glosses: A metallic salt derived from a fatty acid, commonly used in cleaning products.
Some other substance, often a detergent or another surfactant, able to mix with both oil and water, used for cleaning.

examples.text: I tried washing my hands with soap, but the stain wouldn't go away.
She went to the shop to buy soap, but they had run out.

glosses: Money, specially when used as a bribe.
A solid masonry unit or brick reduced in depth or height from standard dimensions.
To apply soap to in washing.

examples.text: Be sure to soap yourself well before rinsing.

glosses: To cover, lather, or in any other manner treat with soap, often as a prank.

examples.text: 'Time? Doesn't have much meaning when they're trying to dry you out. I rather think they gave me a shot of soap at one point.' Soap is intelligence speak for sodium pentathol.

glosses: Restregar un objeto (vajilla, ropa, etc.) con jabón y agua para limpiarlo o ablandarlo.

examples.text: Se lavaban la cara por las fiestas, y el cuerpo nunca, a pesar de que tenían a orgullo llevar muy limpios sus pañuelos, sus faldas, sus corpiños, lo cual hacíalas pasarse enjabonando ropas todo el día.

glosses: Frotar la piel o el cabello con jabón y agua.

examples.text: se frotaba las manos con fuerza y como si se las estuviera enjabonando en seco
